rationale.conceptual: The paper employs established density functional perturbation theory (DFPT) and Allen-Dynes formula for superconductivity. While not a new algorithm, correct implementation requires understanding of electron-phonon coupling, integration of Eliashberg function, and the physics of the material system. This is a non-trivial but well-documented method.
rationale.execution: The workflow comprises geometry optimizations, DFPT phonon calculations on a dense q-grid, and postprocessing to extract α²F(ω) and derived quantities, using multiple QuantumESPRESSO tools (pw.x, ph.x, q2r.x, etc.). The pipeline has multiple sequential stages with interdependencies and non-trivial data handling (phonon modes, electron-phonon matrix elements), but no extreme orchestration or data acquisition.

difficulty.reasoning: The task involves reproducing electron-phonon coupling results from a first-principles DFT/DFPT study. The method (DFT+DFPT) is standard but non-trivial; the pipeline has multiple stages with dependencies. Resource needs are CPU-based, moderate memory, and long runtime.

compute_estimate.reasoning: The main computational load is DFPT phonon calculations on 24×24×1 q-grids for two systems with plane-wave cutoff 70 Ryd. This is CPU-intensive (many hours) but not memory-heavy; estimated peak RAM ~16 GB. Input and output data volume is small (structure files, pseudopotentials, spectral arrays).
